1.1Cron Substrate — System Reference

Cron Substrate — system reference
What it is, what it stores, and every surface a reader can touch.

The cron substrate is a session-scoped, in-memory job scheduler exposed to every citizen through three calls: CronCreate, CronList, CronDelete. It stores no state on disk and vanishes when the session ends.

  • jobs (in-memory)job id, cron expression, prompt, recurring flag, created-at
  • no persistent tablenothing survives a session restart — this is the root cause behind most findings in the companion report
job record

One entry per CronCreate call, held in the session's in-memory table.

  • idopaque job id, returned to caller
  • cron5-field cron expression, local time
  • prompttext enqueued at each fire
  • recurringbool — false auto-deletes after first fire
The dashed edge is the one path with no caller in the loop — this is the shape a reader needs before they trust the table above.
